name: Otterly v0.7.0
body:
## New

- Updates show their progress in the status bar: checking, then the download with megabytes and percent, then a "Restart to update" button. Checking by hand from the command palette no longer shows a loading toast.
- Windows portable zip: put `otterly.exe` anywhere you can write to and its settings, vault list, logs and WebView data stay in a `data` folder next to it. A portable copy never updates itself or registers anything with Windows, and it runs side by side with an installed one.
- Windows taskbar jump list and Linux app menu get a New Window entry. New Window also has a hotkey: Ctrl+Shift+N (Shift+Cmd+N on macOS).

## Fixes

- Files changed outside Otterly (by git, a sync tool or another editor) now update search, links and tags, not only the file tree. Renames are followed instead of showing up as a delete and a new file.
- Windows: images in notes load again. Saving no longer fails now and then with "the file is in use" while antivirus or a sync tool has the file open, since every write is atomic and retries.
- Windows: a junction or symlink loop in a vault no longer hangs the scan. `desktop.ini` and `Thumbs.db` stay out of the file tree.
- Windows: a new window started from the taskbar or the jump list comes to the front instead of flashing in the taskbar.
- Vim mode on Windows and Linux: Ctrl+W in insert mode deletes a word instead of closing the tab.
- Restoring a session skips a tab whose file is gone instead of dropping all of them. A note deleted outside the app shows a clear message.
- The search index is released when a window closes, so reopening the vault in another window works straight away.

## Installing and uninstalling on Windows

- The installer asks to close a running Otterly instead of killing it without warning.
- Uninstalling a `setup.exe` install gives `.md` files back to the app that opened them before, and "Also delete settings and the vault list" removes every file and registry key Otterly made. Updating keeps your file association.
- The `.msi` keeps a fixed upgrade code, so each new `.msi` upgrades the old one in place.
- Each install type updates itself from its own package (`setup.exe` from `setup.exe`, `.msi` from `.msi`, `.deb` from `.deb`, AppImage from AppImage).
- The app is called "Otterly" everywhere: Start menu, Settings > Apps, window titles and "Open with".

## Code signing

Otterly has applied to the SignPath Foundation for free code signing for open source. Until that is approved, Windows may still show "Windows protected your PC". Click "More info" and then "Run anyway". See the [code signing policy](https://github.com/ajkdrag/otterly#code-signing-policy).

name: Otterly v0.6.0
body:
Desktop release for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

## What's new

- **Tags.** Type `#tag` in a note and it renders as a styled chip, with autocomplete. `Cmd+T` opens tag search in the omnibar. Pick tags as chips, a note must carry every chip, and anything you type searches inside those notes. There is also a Tags pane in the left bar with counts, a filter box and a note drill-down. A note's own tags show in its side panel. Tags in code, headings and URLs are ignored. Unicode and emoji tags work, and so do frontmatter `tags:`.
- **Find in files, inside Cmd+O.** `Cmd+Shift+F` opens the omnibar in Text mode: regex, case and whole-word toggles, include and exclude globs, and results streamed in grouped by file. Press `Tab` for Replace, with an inline preview. You can replace one match, a file, or everything, behind a confirm dialog. Tag chips scope a find, so "replace foo only in notes tagged #project" is one flow. Vaults that are not git repos get a warning, because replace cannot be undone there.
- **Theme file.** Edit `theme.yaml` or `theme.json` in the app config folder and the whole app restyles live. Errors name the line, and a JSON schema is written next to the file for editors and coding agents. It covers colors, fonts, spacing, radius, tree density, headings, quotes, code, tables and tag chips, plus raw CSS tokens. Settings > Theme shows the path.
- **Vim mode.** Turn it on in Settings > Vim. Motions, operators, counts, text objects, visual modes, registers, search, macros and a small ex set, checked against real `vim`. You get a mode indicator, a cursor shape per mode and a pending-key display. A `vimrc` in the app config folder takes `map` variants and `set`, and lines that do not apply are listed with line numbers in Settings.
- **New windows.** `Shift+Cmd+N`, File > New Window and the Dock menu open another window. A vault can open in this window or in a new one, from the window button on a picker row or `Cmd+Enter` in the switcher. A vault is open in at most one window, and opening it again focuses that window. Settings are shared.
- **Windows portable zip**, next to the installer. It skips the installer updater.
- **Standalone file windows** got find, word counts, copy, reveal and help.

## Changed

- `Cmd+Shift+F` is now find in files. "Search All Vaults" moved to `Cmd+Alt+Shift+F`.
- The vault window and the standalone file window share one status bar.
- The omnibar tabs are `All | Files | Text`. The old content-only tab and the `@content` prefix are gone, and `Text` is exact search.

## Fixed

- AppImage builds ship a working `.DirIcon`, and CI checks it.

The Windows and Linux builds are fresh in this release and have had less hands-on testing than macOS. Please report anything odd.

name: v0.5.0 - Source-Preserving Editor

name: Otterly v0.4.1
body:
Otterly v0.4.1 is ready for macOS, Windows, and Linux. [Watch the tour](https://ajkdrag.github.io/otterly/) if you want to see the app first.

## Download

- [Mac with Apple Silicon](https://github.com/ajkdrag/otterly/releases/download/v0.4.1/otterly_0.4.1_aarch64.dmg)
- [Mac with Intel](https://github.com/ajkdrag/otterly/releases/download/v0.4.1/otterly_0.4.1_x64.dmg)
- [Windows installer](https://github.com/ajkdrag/otterly/releases/download/v0.4.1/otterly_0.4.1_x64-setup.exe)
- [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/ajkdrag/otterly/releases/download/v0.4.1/otterly_0.4.1_amd64.AppImage) or [Debian package](https://github.com/ajkdrag/otterly/releases/download/v0.4.1/otterly_0.4.1_amd64.deb)

The Mac build is not notarized yet, so macOS may show a warning when you first open it.

## New

- **Automatic updates.** Otterly now checks for updates in the background and downloads them for you. When one is ready you get a prompt: **Restart** installs it and reopens Otterly with your tabs, **Later** stops asking for the rest of the session. "Check for Updates" in the command palette still works any time.
  - This starts with this version. If you are on v0.4.0, update by hand one last time.
- **Open linked files** ([#28](https://github.com/ajkdrag/otterly/issues/28)). Click a link to a non-note file in a note, like `[budget](files/budget.xlsx)`, and it opens in its default app. Paths are relative to the note, the same as images. For safety, links to programs and scripts (`.exe`, `.command`, `.sh` and similar) do not open. Use Reveal in Finder for those.
- **Open in Default App** is now in the tab right-click menu too, next to Reveal in Finder.

## Fixed

- Mermaid diagrams switch to the new colors right away when you change between light and dark themes. Before, they kept the old theme until you edited the diagram or reopened the note.

## Improved

- A smaller app. We dropped some unused native libraries, which also makes releases build faster.

name: Otterly v0.4.0
body:
Desktop release for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

## New

- **Mermaid diagrams** ([#26](https://github.com/ajkdrag/otterly/issues/26)). A ` ```mermaid ` code block now renders as a diagram under its source. You can:
  - zoom from 25% to 1000% (click the percentage to fit the width again),
  - hide the source and keep only the diagram,
  - resize the source and the diagram separately.

  Otterly remembers these per block. Pick "Mermaid" in the code block language picker to turn an existing block into a diagram.
- **Reveal in Finder** ([#27](https://github.com/ajkdrag/otterly/issues/27)). Right-click a note or folder in the file tree, or a tab, and pick "Reveal in Finder" ("Show in Explorer" on Windows, "Show in File Manager" on Linux). Notes in the file tree also get "Open in Default App".
- **Editor zoom.** `Cmd/Ctrl` + `=` zooms in, `Cmd/Ctrl` + `-` zooms out, and `Cmd/Ctrl` + `0` resets. You can rebind them in Settings > Hotkeys, and the zoom level is kept across restarts.
- The `+` key can now be used in custom hotkeys.

## Improved

- More reliable editing of code blocks, lists and task lists, and fixes to autosave.
- A more consistent look across themes, the vault dashboard, search and the command palette. Fonts are now bundled with the app.
- The command palette shows shortcuts as key caps, like the rest of the app.
- The sidebar "New note" button is easier to spot.

## Docs

- Arch Linux install via the AUR ([#30](https://github.com/ajkdrag/otterly/pull/30), thanks @Cleboost).

## Heads up

- Code block heights you set in earlier versions reset once after updating.
